publications.explanation:
B, only argument II is strong, under the printed test of importance and direct relevance. Argument I calls free schooling the only way to improve literacy, an unsupported absolute claim. Argument II raises the cost to public finances, which is a substantial consideration directly related to funding free schooling.

This classifies arguments; it does not decide whether free schooling is desirable or establish the actual budget impact. Calling an argument strong means it deserves consideration under the question's rubric, not that it outweighs every educational benefit.

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'B'..pdf
publications.explanation:
A, Kyoto Protocol, is the intended answer. Kyoto established international market mechanisms involving tradable emissions units and project-based credits. Its Clean Development Mechanism could issue certified emission reductions, while international emissions trading allowed transfers of eligible units. This is the historical treaty framework being tested; the wording should not be read as claiming that every form of environmental credit trading began there. [UNFCCC, Emissions Trading](https://unfccc.int/process/the-kyoto-protocol/mechanisms/emissions-trading).

Update — checked 21 November 2026: A UNFCCC notice dated 12 December 2025 scheduled cessation of the Kyoto International Transaction Log for 31 March 2026. This concerns Kyoto registry infrastructure, not the end of all carbon markets. It does not change the historical answer. [UNFCCC, Registry Systems](https://unfccc.int/process/the-kyoto-protocol/registry-systems).

publications.paper_id: Old_Questions/Direct_2023-2025/MCS Combined 2023 Preliminary Exam Paper-I Series 'A'.pdf
publications.explanation: A, ritual bath. NCERT explains that the Great Bath's unusual structure and its setting among distinctive buildings on the Citadel led scholars to suggest a special ritual purpose. The tank had steps, watertight construction and drainage, but these features alone do not prove exactly which ceremonies occurred. Notice the question's wording: “scholars suggested” asks for an archaeological interpretation, not a directly documented certainty or evidence of a diving competition. [NCERT, Themes in Indian History I, section 3.3, page 8](https://ncert.nic.in/textbook/pdf/lehs101.pdf).
